   119→
   120→class VEXParser:
   121→    """Parse VEX code from various sources."""
   122→
   123→    # Regex patterns for VEX extraction
   124→    WRANGLE_PATTERN = re.compile(
   125→        r'(?:^|\n)\s*//\s*(?:VEX|wrangle|Wrangle)[^\n]*\n(.*?)(?=\n\s*//|\Z)',
   126→        re.DOTALL
   127→    )
   128→
   129→    CODE_BLOCK_PATTERN = re.compile(
   130→        r'```(?:vex|c\+\+|cpp)?\n(.*?)```',
   131→        re.DOTALL
   132→    )
   133→
   134→    @classmethod
   135→    def extract_from_file(cls, file_path: Path) -> list[VEXSample]:
   136→        """Extract VEX samples from a file."""
   137→        samples = []
   138→        content = file_path.read_text(encoding='utf-8', errors='replace')
   139→
   140→        if file_path.suffix in ('.vex', '.h', '.vfl'):
   141→            # Raw VEX file - treat entire content as one sample
   142→            samples.append(VEXSample(
   143→                id="",
   144→                code=content.strip(),
   145→                source_file=str(file_path),
   146→                source_line=1,
   147→            ))
   148→        elif file_path.suffix in ('.hip', '.hipnc', '.hiplc'):
   149→            # Houdini file - would need proper parsing
   150→            # For now, skip binary files
   151→            pass
   152→        elif file_path.suffix in ('.md', '.txt'):
   153→            # Markdown/text - extract code blocks
   154→            for match in cls.CODE_BLOCK_PATTERN.finditer(content):
   155→                code = match.group(1).strip()
   156→                if cls._looks_like_vex(code):
   157→                    line_num = content[:match.start()].count('\n') + 1
   158→                    samples.append(VEXSample(
   159→                        id="",
   160→                        code=code,
   161→                        source_file=str(file_path),
   162→                        source_line=line_num,
   163→                    ))
   164→        elif file_path.suffix == '.json':
   165→            # JSON - look for code fields
   166→            try:
   167→                data = json.loads(content)
   168→                samples.extend(cls._extract_from_json(data, str(file_path)))
   169→            except json.JSONDecodeError:
   170→                pass
   171→
   172→        return samples
   173→
   174→    @classmethod
   175→    def _looks_like_vex(cls, code: str) -> bool:
   176→        """Check if code looks like VEX."""
   177→        vex_indicators = [
   178→            '@P', '@N', '@Cd', '@ptnum', '@primnum',
   179→            'ch(', 'chf(', 'chi(', 'chv(',
   180→            'point(', 'prim(', 'setpointattrib(',
   181→            'pcopen(', 'pcfind(', 'nearpoints(',
   182→            'vector ', 'float ', 'int ',
   183→        ]
   184→        return any(ind in code for ind in vex_indicators)
   185→
   186→    @classmethod
   187→    def _extract_from_json(cls, data: Any, source: str, samples: list = None) -> list[VEXSample]:
   188→        """Recursively extract VEX from JSON data."""
   189→        if samples is None:
   190→            samples = []
   191→
   192→        if isinstance(data, dict):
   193→            for key, value in data.items():
   194→                if key in ('code', 'vex', 'vex_code', 'snippet') and isinstance(value, str):
   195→                    if cls._looks_like_vex(value):
   196→                        samples.append(VEXSample(
   197→                            id=data.get('id', ''),
   198→                            code=value.strip(),
   199→                            source_file=source,
   200→                        ))
   201→                else:
   202→                    cls._extract_from_json(value, source, samples)
   203→        elif isinstance(data, list):
   204→            for item in data:
   205→                cls._extract_from_json(item, source, samples)
   206→
   207→        return samples
   208→
   209→
   210→class IntakePipeline:
   211→    """Main intake pipeline for VEX corpus processing."""
   212→
   213→    def __init__(
   214→        self,
   215→        output_dir: Path = None,
   216→        tier1_concurrency: int = 5,
   217→        tier2_concurrency: int = 2,
   218→    ):
   219→        self.output_dir = output_dir or Path("C:/Users/User/vex-corpus/output")
   220→        self.output_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
   221→
   222→        self.client = OllamaClient()
   223→        self.dispatcher = TaskDispatcher(client=self.client)
   224→
   225→        self.tier1_concurrency = tier1_concurrency
   226→        self.tier2_concurrency = tier2_concurrency
   227→
   228→        self.samples: dict[str, VEXSample] = {}
   229→        self.processed_hashes: set[str] = set()
   230→
   231→        # Callbacks
   232→        self._on_progress: Callable[[str, int, int], None] | None = None
   233→        self._on_sample_complete: Callable[[VEXSample], None] | None = None
   234→        self._on_error: Callable[[str, Exception], None] | None = None
   235→
   236→    def on_progress(self, callback: Callable[[str, int, int], None]):
   237→        """Register progress callback (stage, current, total)."""
   238→        self._on_progress = callback
   239→
   240→    def on_sample_complete(self, callback: Callable[[VEXSample], None]):
   241→        """Register sample completion callback."""
   242→        self._on_sample_complete = callback
   243→
   244→    def on_error(self, callback: Callable[[str, Exception], None]):
   245→        """Register error callback."""
   246→        self._on_error = callback
   247→
   248→    def _report_progress(self, stage: str, current: int, total: int):
   249→        if self._on_progress:
   250→            self._on_progress(stage, current, total)
   251→
   252→    async def ingest_file(self, file_path: Path) -> list[VEXSample]:
   253→        """Ingest VEX samples from a file."""
   254→        samples = VEXParser.extract_from_file(file_path)
   255→
   256→        # Deduplicate
   257→        new_samples = []
   258→        for sample in samples:
   259→            if sample.hash not in self.processed_hashes:
   260→                self.samples[sample.id] = sample
   261→                self.processed_hashes.add(sample.hash)
   262→                new_samples.append(sample)
   263→
   264→        return new_samples
   265→
   266→    async def ingest_directory(self, dir_path: Path, recursive: bool = True) -> list[VEXSample]:
   267→        """Ingest all VEX files from a directory."""
   268→        all_samples = []
   269→
   270→        pattern = "**/*" if recursive else "*"
   271→        extensions = {'.vex', '.vfl', '.h', '.md', '.txt', '.json'}
   272→
   273→        files = [f for f in dir_path.glob(pattern) if f.suffix in extensions]
   274→
   275→        for i, file_path in enumerate(files):
   276→            self._report_progress("Ingesting files", i + 1, len(files))
   277→            try:
   278→                samples = await self.ingest_file(file_path)
   279→                all_samples.extend(samples)
   280→            except Exception as e:
   281→                if self._on_error:
   282→                    self._on_error(str(file_path), e)
   283→
   284→        return all_samples
   285→
   286→    async def ingest_code(self, code: str, source: str = "direct_input") -> VEXSample:
   287→        """Ingest a single VEX code string."""
   288→        sample = VEXSample(id="", code=code, source_file=source)
   289→
   290→        if sample.hash not in self.processed_hashes:
   291→            self.samples[sample.id] = sample
   292→            self.processed_hashes.add(sample.hash)
   293→
   294→        return sample
   295→
   296→    async def process_tier1(self, samples: list[VEXSample]) -> list[VEXSample]:
   297→        """Run Tier 1 classification tasks on samples."""
   298→        tier1_tasks = [
   299→            "classify_wrangle",
   300→            "extract_attributes",
   301→            "extract_functions",
   302→            "detect_bugs",
   303→            "estimate_complexity",
   304→            "classify_topic",
   305→        ]
   306→
   307→        total = len(samples) * len(tier1_tasks)
   308→        completed = 0
   309→
   310→        # Semaphore to limit concurrent Ollama requests (prevents timeouts)
   311→        sem = asyncio.Semaphore(2)
   312→
   313→        async def run_with_limit(task_type, code, task_id):
   314→            async with sem:
   315→                return await self.dispatcher.dispatch(task_type, {"code": code}, task_id=task_id)
   316→
   317→        for sample in samples:
   318→            sample.stage = ProcessingStage.TIER1_CLASSIFICATION
   319→
   320→            # Run tier1 tasks with limited concurrency
   321→            tasks = []
   322→            for task_type in tier1_tasks:
   323→                tasks.append(run_with_limit(
   324→                    task_type,
   325→                    sample.code,
   326→                    f"{sample.id}_{task_type}"
   327→                ))
   328→
   329→            results = await asyncio.gather(*tasks, return_exceptions=True)
   330→
   331→            # Process results
   332→            for task_type, result in zip(tier1_tasks, results):
   333→                completed += 1
   334→                self._report_progress("Tier 1 Classification", completed, total)
   335→
   336→                if isinstance(result, Exception):
   337→                    continue
   338→
   339→                if result.status != TaskStatus.SUCCESS:
   340→                    continue
   341→
   342→                r = result.result
   343→
   344→                if task_type == "classify_wrangle":
   345→                    sample.context = r.get("context", "unknown")
   346→                    sample.context_confidence = result.confidence
   347→                elif task_type == "extract_attributes":
   348→                    sample.attributes_read = r.get("reads", [])
   349→                    sample.attributes_written = r.get("writes", [])
   350→                    sample.channels = r.get("channels", [])
   351→                elif task_type == "extract_functions":
   352→                    sample.functions = r.get("functions", [])
   353→                elif task_type == "detect_bugs":
   354→                    sample.bugs = r.get("bugs", [])
   355→                elif task_type == "estimate_complexity":
   356→                    sample.complexity = r.get("complexity", "")
   357→                elif task_type == "classify_topic":
   358→                    sample.topic = r.get("primary_topic", "")
   359→
   360→            # Check for review flags
   361→            if sample.context_confidence < 0.6:
   362→                sample.flagged_for_review = True
   363→                sample.review_reason = f"Low context confidence: {sample.context_confidence:.2f}"
   364→
   365→        return samples
   366→
   367→    async def process_tier2(self, samples: list[VEXSample]) -> list[VEXSample]:
   368→        """Run Tier 2 generation tasks on samples."""
   369→        tier2_tasks = [
   370→            "generate_prompt",
   371→            "generate_explanation",
   372→            "rate_difficulty",
   373→        ]
   374→
   375→        total = len(samples) * len(tier2_tasks)
   376→        completed = 0
   377→
   378→        for sample in samples:
   379→            sample.stage = ProcessingStage.TIER2_GENERATION
   380→
   381→            # Run tier2 tasks (sequentially to avoid overload)
   382→            for task_type in tier2_tasks:
   383→                completed += 1
   384→                self._report_progress("Tier 2 Generation", completed, total)
   385→
   386→                try:
   387→                    input_data = {"code": sample.code}
   388→                    if task_type == "generate_explanation":
   389→                        input_data["audience"] = "intermediate"
   390→                        input_data["task"] = sample.topic or "VEX operation"
   391→
   392→                    result = await self.dispatcher.dispatch(
   393→                        task_type,
   394→                        input_data,
   395→                        task_id=f"{sample.id}_{task_type}"
   396→                    )
   397→
   398→                    if result.status != TaskStatus.SUCCESS:
   399→                        continue
   400→
   401→                    r = result.result
   402→
   403→                    if task_type == "generate_prompt":
   404→                        sample.prompt = r.get("prompt", "")
   405→                        sample.alternative_prompts = r.get("alternative_phrasings", [])
   406→                    elif task_type == "generate_explanation":
   407→                        sample.explanation = r.get("explanation", "")
   408→                    elif task_type == "rate_difficulty":
   409→                        sample.difficulty = r.get("difficulty", 0)
   410→
   411→                except Exception as e:
   412→                    if self._on_error:
   413→                        self._on_error(f"{sample.id}_{task_type}", e)
   414→
   415→            sample.stage = ProcessingStage.COMPLETE
   416→
   417→            if self._on_sample_complete:
   418→                self._on_sample_complete(sample)
   419→
   420→        return samples
   421→
   422→    async def process_all(self, samples: list[VEXSample] = None) -> list[VEXSample]:
   423→        """Process all samples through the full pipeline."""
   424→        if samples is None:
   425→            samples = list(self.samples.values())
   426→
   427→        # Filter to only pending samples
   428→        pending = [s for s in samples if s.stage == ProcessingStage.PENDING]
   429→
   430→        if not pending:
   431→            return []
   432→
   433→        # Tier 1
   434→        await self.process_tier1(pending)
   435→
   436→        # Tier 2 (only for samples that passed tier 1)
   437→        tier2_candidates = [s for s in pending if not s.flagged_for_review]
   438→        await self.process_tier2(tier2_candidates)
   439→
   440→        return pending
   441→
   442→    def export_corpus(self, output_path: Path = None) -> Path:
   443→        """Export processed corpus to JSON."""
   444→        if output_path is None:
   445→            timestamp = datetime.now().strftime("%Y%m%d_%H%M%S")
   446→            output_path = self.output_dir / f"vex_corpus_{timestamp}.json"
   447→
   448→        completed = [s for s in self.samples.values() if s.stage == ProcessingStage.COMPLETE]
   449→
   450→        corpus = {
   451→            "metadata": {
   452→                "generated_at": datetime.now().isoformat(),
   453→                "total_samples": len(completed),
   454→                "flagged_for_review": sum(1 for s in completed if s.flagged_for_review),
   455→            },
   456→            "samples": [s.to_dict() for s in completed],
   457→        }
   458→
   459→        with open(output_path, 'w', encoding='utf-8') as f:
   460→            json.dump(corpus, f, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False)
   461→
   462→        return output_path
   463→
   464→    def export_training_data(self, output_path: Path = None) -> Path:
   465→        """Export as training pairs (prompt, completion)."""
   466→        if output_path is None:
   467→            timestamp = datetime.now().strftime("%Y%m%d_%H%M%S")
   468→            output_path = self.output_dir / f"training_data_{timestamp}.jsonl"
   469→
   470→        with open(output_path, 'w', encoding='utf-8') as f:
   471→            for sample in self.samples.values():
   472→                pair = sample.to_training_pair()
   473→                if pair:
   474→                    f.write(json.dumps(pair, ensure_ascii=False) + '\n')
   475→
   476→        return output_path
   477→
   478→    def get_stats(self) -> dict:
   479→        """Get processing statistics."""
   480→        samples = list(self.samples.values())
   481→
   482→        by_stage = {}
   483→        for stage in ProcessingStage:
   484→            by_stage[stage.value] = sum(1 for s in samples if s.stage == stage)
   485→
   486→        by_context = {}
   487→        for s in samples:
   488→            ctx = s.context or "unknown"
   489→            by_context[ctx] = by_context.get(ctx, 0) + 1
   490→
   491→        by_topic = {}
   492→        for s in samples:
   493→            topic = s.topic or "unknown"
   494→            by_topic[topic] = by_topic.get(topic, 0) + 1
   495→
   496→        return {
   497→            "total": len(samples),
   498→            "by_stage": by_stage,
   499→            "by_context": by_context,
   500→            "by_topic": by_topic,
   501→            "flagged_for_review": sum(1 for s in samples if s.flagged_for_review),
   502→            "with_prompts": sum(1 for s in samples if s.prompt),
   503→        }
   504→

1→"""File watcher for automatic VEX file ingestion."""
     2→
     3→import asyncio
     4→import time
     5→from pathlib import Path
     6→from typing import Callable, Optional
     7→from dataclasses import dataclass
     8→from datetime import datetime
     9→
    10→
    11→@dataclass
    12→class FileEvent:
    13→    """A file system event."""
    14→    path: Path
    15→    event_type: str  # created, modified, deleted
    16→    timestamp: datetime
    17→
    18→
    19→class VEXFileWatcher:
    20→    """Watch directories for new VEX files."""
    21→
    22→    EXTENSIONS = {'.vex', '.vfl', '.h', '.md', '.txt', '.json'}
    23→
    24→    def __init__(
    25→        self,
    26→        directories: list[Path],
    27→        on_file: Callable[[Path], None],
    28→        poll_interval: float = 2.0,
    29→    ):
    30→        self.directories = directories
    31→        self.on_file = on_file
    32→        self.poll_interval = poll_interval
    33→
    34→        self._running = False
    35→        self._seen_files: dict[Path, float] = {}  # path -> mtime
    36→        self._task: Optional[asyncio.Task] = None
    37→
    38→    def _scan_directory(self, directory: Path) -> list[FileEvent]:
    39→        """Scan a directory for new/modified files."""
    40→        events = []
    41→
    42→        for ext in self.EXTENSIONS:
    43→            for file_path in directory.rglob(f"*{ext}"):
    44→                try:
    45→                    mtime = file_path.stat().st_mtime
    46→                    prev_mtime = self._seen_files.get(file_path)
    47→
    48→                    if prev_mtime is None:
    49→                        # New file
    50→                        events.append(FileEvent(
    51→                            path=file_path,
    52→                            event_type="created",
    53→                            timestamp=datetime.now()
    54→                        ))
    55→                    elif mtime > prev_mtime:
    56→                        # Modified file
    57→                        events.append(FileEvent(
    58→                            path=file_path,
    59→                            event_type="modified",
    60→                            timestamp=datetime.now()
    61→                        ))
    62→
    63→                    self._seen_files[file_path] = mtime
    64→
    65→                except (OSError, PermissionError):
    66→                    continue
    67→
    68→        return events
    69→
    70→    async def _watch_loop(self):
    71→        """Main watch loop."""
    72→        # Initial scan - just record files without triggering events
    73→        for directory in self.directories:
    74→            if directory.exists():
    75→                for ext in self.EXTENSIONS:
    76→                    for file_path in directory.rglob(f"*{ext}"):
    77→                        try:
    78→                            self._seen_files[file_path] = file_path.stat().st_mtime
    79→                        except (OSError, PermissionError):
    80→                            continue
    81→
    82→        # Watch loop
    83→        while self._running:
    84→            for directory in self.directories:
    85→                if not directory.exists():
    86→                    continue
    87→
    88→                events = self._scan_directory(directory)
    89→
    90→                for event in events:
    91→                    if event.event_type in ("created", "modified"):
    92→                        try:
    93→                            self.on_file(event.path)
    94→                        except Exception:
    95→                            pass
    96→
    97→            await asyncio.sleep(self.poll_interval)
    98→
    99→    def start(self):
   100→        """Start watching."""
   101→        if self._running:
   102→            return
   103→
   104→        self._running = True
   105→        self._task = asyncio.create_task(self._watch_loop())
   106→
   107→    def stop(self):
   108→        """Stop watching."""
   109→        self._running = False
   110→        if self._task:
   111→            self._task.cancel()
   112→            self._task = None
   113→
   114→    def add_directory(self, directory: Path):
   115→        """Add a directory to watch."""
   116→        if directory not in self.directories:
   117→            self.directories.append(directory)
   118→
   119→    def remove_directory(self, directory: Path):
   120→        """Remove a directory from watch list."""
   121→        if directory in self.directories:
   122→            self.directories.remove(directory)
   123→
   124→
   125→class BatchAccumulator:
   126→    """Accumulate files into batches before processing."""
   127→
   128→    def __init__(
   129→        self,
   130→        on_batch: Callable[[list[Path]], None],
   131→        batch_size: int = 10,
   132→        max_wait: float = 30.0,
   133→    ):
   134→        self.on_batch = on_batch
   135→        self.batch_size = batch_size
   136→        self.max_wait = max_wait
   137→
   138→        self._pending: list[Path] = []
   139→        self._last_add: float = 0
   140→        self._task: Optional[asyncio.Task] = None
   141→        self._running = False
   142→
   143→    def add(self, path: Path):
   144→        """Add a file to the batch."""
   145→        if path not in self._pending:
   146→            self._pending.append(path)
   147→            self._last_add = time.time()
   148→
   149→        # Trigger if batch is full
   150→        if len(self._pending) >= self.batch_size:
   151→            self._flush()
   152→
   153→    def _flush(self):
   154→        """Flush pending files to callback."""
   155→        if self._pending:
   156→            batch = self._pending.copy()
   157→            self._pending.clear()
   158→            try:
   159→                self.on_batch(batch)
   160→            except Exception:
   161→                pass
   162→
   163→    async def _timer_loop(self):
   164→        """Timer loop to flush after max_wait."""
   165→        while self._running:
   166→            await asyncio.sleep(1.0)
   167→
   168→            if self._pending and (time.time() - self._last_add) >= self.max_wait:
   169→                self._flush()
   170→
   171→    def start(self):
   172→        """Start the timer."""
   173→        if self._running:
   174→            return
   175→        self._running = True
   176→        self._task = asyncio.create_task(self._timer_loop())
   177→
   178→    def stop(self):
   179→        """Stop and flush remaining."""
   180→        self._running = False
   181→        if self._task:
   182→            self._task.cancel()
   183→            self._task = None
   184→        self._flush()
   185→

1→"""Async Ollama client for VEX corpus processing."""
     2→
     3→import json
     4→from pathlib import Path
     5→from typing import Any
     6→
     7→import httpx
     8→import yaml
     9→from pydantic import BaseModel
    10→
    11→from .models import TaskResult, TaskStatus
    12→
    13→
    14→class ModelConfig(BaseModel):
    15→    """Configuration for a model tier."""
    16→
    17→    primary: str
    18→    fallbacks: list[str] = []
    19→    config: dict[str, Any] = {}
    20→
    21→
    22→class OllamaClient:
    23→    """Async client for Ollama API with VEX corpus processing support."""
    24→
    25→    def __init__(
    26→        self,
    27→        base_url: str = "http://localhost:11434",
    28→        config_path: Path | None = None,
    29→    ):
    30→        self.base_url = base_url.rstrip("/")
    31→        self.config = self._load_config(config_path)
    32→        self._blueprint: str | None = None
    33→
    34→    def _load_config(self, config_path: Path | None) -> dict[str, Any]:
    35→        """Load configuration from YAML file."""
    36→        if config_path is None:
    37→            config_path = Path(__file__).parent.parent.parent / "config" / "models.yaml"
    38→
    39→        if config_path.exists():
    40→            with open(config_path) as f:
    41→                return yaml.safe_load(f)
    42→        return {}
    43→
    44→    def load_blueprint(self, blueprint_path: Path | None = None) -> str:
    45→        """Load the VEX processing blueprint as system prompt."""
    46→        if blueprint_path is None:
    47→            blueprint_path = (
    48→                Path(__file__).parent.parent.parent
    49→                / "blueprints"
    50→                / "OLLAMA_PROCESSING_BLUEPRINT.md"
    51→            )
    52→
    53→        if blueprint_path.exists():
    54→            self._blueprint = blueprint_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
    55→        return self._blueprint or ""
    56→
    57→    @property
    58→    def blueprint(self) -> str:
    59→        """Get the loaded blueprint, loading if necessary."""
    60→        if self._blueprint is None:
    61→            self.load_blueprint()
    62→        return self._blueprint or ""
    63→
    64→    def get_model_for_tier(self, tier: int) -> ModelConfig:
    65→        """Get model configuration for the specified tier."""
    66→        tier_key = f"tier{tier}"
    67→        tier_config = self.config.get("models", {}).get(tier_key, {})
    68→        return ModelConfig(
    69→            primary=tier_config.get("primary", "nemotron-mini:latest"),
    70→            fallbacks=tier_config.get("fallbacks", []),
    71→            config=tier_config.get("config", {}),
    72→        )
    73→
    74→    async def health_check(self) -> dict[str, Any]:
    75→        """Check Ollama server health and available models."""
    76→        async with httpx.AsyncClient() as client:
    77→            try:
    78→                response = await client.get(f"{self.base_url}/api/tags", timeout=10.0)
    79→                response.raise_for_status()
    80→                data = response.json()
    81→
    82→                models = data.get("models", [])
    83→                available = {m["name"].split(":")[0] for m in models}
    84→
    85→                required = {"nemotron-mini", "nemotron"}
    86→                missing = required - available
    87→
    88→                return {
    89→                    "status": "healthy" if not missing else "degraded",
    90→                    "available_models": sorted(available),
    91→                    "missing_models": sorted(missing),
    92→                    "model_count": len(models),
    93→                }
    94→            except httpx.RequestError as e:
    95→                return {
    96→                    "status": "offline",
    97→                    "error": str(e),
    98→                    "available_models": [],
    99→                    "missing_models": [],
   100→                }
   101→
   102→    async def generate(
   103→        self,
   104→        model: str,
   105→        prompt: str,
   106→        system: str | None = None,
   107→        options: dict[str, Any] | None = None,
   108→        timeout: float = 60.0,
   109→    ) -> dict[str, Any]:
   110→        """Send a generate request to Ollama."""
   111→        payload: dict[str, Any] = {
   112→            "model": model,
   113→            "prompt": prompt,
   114→            "stream": False,
   115→        }
   116→
   117→        if system:
   118→            payload["system"] = system
   119→
   120→        if options:
   121→            payload["options"] = options
   122→            if "format" in options:
   123→                payload["format"] = options.pop("format")
   124→
   125→        async with httpx.AsyncClient() as client:
   126→            response = await client.post(
   127→                f"{self.base_url}/api/generate",
   128→                json=payload,
   129→                timeout=timeout,
   130→            )
   131→            response.raise_for_status()
   132→            return response.json()
   133→
   134→    async def process_task(
   135→        self,
   136→        task_type: str,
   137→        input_data: dict[str, Any],
   138→        task_id: str = "",
   139→        model: str | None = None,
   140→        use_focused_prompt: bool = True,
   141→    ) -> TaskResult:
   142→        """Process a VEX task using the appropriate model."""
   143→        from .models import TIER1_TASKS, TIER2_TASKS, TaskType
   144→        from .prompts import get_task_prompt
   145→
   146→        # Determine tier and model
   147→        try:
   148→            task_enum = TaskType(task_type)
   149→        except ValueError:
   150→            return TaskResult(
   151→                task_id=task_id,
   152→                status=TaskStatus.ERROR,
   153→                result={"error_type": "unknown_task", "error_message": f"Unknown task: {task_type}"},
   154→            )
   155→
   156→        if task_enum in TIER1_TASKS:
   157→            tier = 1
   158→        elif task_enum in TIER2_TASKS:
   159→            tier = 2
   160→        else:
   161→            tier = 1
   162→
   163→        model_config = self.get_model_for_tier(tier)
   164→        selected_model = model or model_config.primary
   165→
   166→        # Get task config - timeouts now properly configured in models.yaml
   167→        task_config = self.config.get("tasks", {}).get(task_type, {})
   168→        timeout = task_config.get("timeout_seconds", 60) * 1.0
   169→
   170→        # Build prompt - include the code directly for better parsing
   171→        code = input_data.get("code", "")
   172→        prompt = f"Task ID: {task_id}\n\nVEX Code:\n```vex\n{code}\n```\n\nAnalyze this VEX code and respond with JSON."
   173→
   174→        # Get system prompt - use focused prompt for better results with smaller models
   175→        if use_focused_prompt:
   176→            system = get_task_prompt(task_type) or self.blueprint
   177→        else:
   178→            system = self.blueprint
   179→
   180→        # Build options from model config
   181→        options = dict(model_config.config)
   182→
   183→        models_to_try = [selected_model] + model_config.fallbacks
   184→
   185→        for i, model_name in enumerate(models_to_try):
   186→            try:
   187→                response = await self.generate(
   188→                    model=model_name,
   189→                    prompt=prompt,
   190→                    system=system,
   191→                    options=options,
   192→                    timeout=timeout,
   193→                )
   194→
   195→                result = self._parse_response(response, task_id)
   196→                result.model_used = model_name
   197→                if i > 0:
   198→                    result.fallback_used = model_name
   199→                return result
   200→
   201→            except httpx.TimeoutException:
   202→                if i < len(models_to_try) - 1:
   203→                    continue
   204→                return TaskResult(
   205→                    task_id=task_id,
   206→                    status=TaskStatus.ERROR,
   207→                    result={"error_type": "timeout", "error_message": "All models timed out"},
   208→                    model_used=model_name,
   209→                )
   210→            except httpx.HTTPStatusError as e:
   211→                if i < len(models_to_try) - 1:
   212→                    continue
   213→                return TaskResult(
   214→                    task_id=task_id,
   215→                    status=TaskStatus.ERROR,
   216→                    result={"error_type": "http_error", "error_message": str(e)},
   217→                    model_used=model_name,
   218→                )
   219→            except Exception as e:
   220→                if i < len(models_to_try) - 1:
   221→                    continue
   222→                return TaskResult(
   223→                    task_id=task_id,
   224→                    status=TaskStatus.ERROR,
   225→                    result={"error_type": "unknown_error", "error_message": str(e)},
   226→                    model_used=model_name,
   227→                )
   228→
   229→        return TaskResult(
   230→            task_id=task_id,
   231→            status=TaskStatus.ERROR,
   232→            result={"error_type": "all_models_failed", "error_message": "No models available"},
   233→        )
   234→
   235→    def _parse_response(self, response: dict[str, Any], task_id: str) -> TaskResult:
   236→        """Parse Ollama response into TaskResult."""
   237→        content = response.get("response", "")
   238→
   239→        # Handle JSON in markdown blocks
   240→        if "```json" in content:
   241→            content = content.split("```json")[1].split("```")[0]
   242→        elif "```" in content:
   243→            content = content.split("```")[1].split("```")[0]
   244→
   245→        content = content.strip()
   246→
   247→        try:
   248→            parsed = json.loads(content)
   249→
   250→            # Extract fields from parsed response
   251→            status_str = parsed.get("status", "success")
   252→            try:
   253→                status = TaskStatus(status_str)
   254→            except ValueError:
   255→                status = TaskStatus.SUCCESS
   256→
   257→            return TaskResult(
   258→                task_id=parsed.get("task_id", task_id),
   259→                status=status,
   260→                result=parsed.get("result", parsed),
   261→                confidence=float(parsed.get("confidence", 0.0)),
   262→                processing_notes=parsed.get("processing_notes", ""),
   263→            )
   264→
   265→        except json.JSONDecodeError:
   266→            return TaskResult(
   267→                task_id=task_id,
   268→                status=TaskStatus.ERROR,
   269→                result={
   270→                    "error_type": "parse_error",
   271→                    "error_message": "Failed to parse JSON response",
   272→                    "raw_response": content[:500],
   273→                },
   274→            )
   275→
   276→    async def list_models(self) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
   277→        """List all available Ollama models."""
   278→        async with httpx.AsyncClient() as client:
   279→            response = await client.get(f"{self.base_url}/api/tags", timeout=10.0)
   280→            response.raise_for_status()
   281→            return response.json().get("models", [])
   282→

1→"""Task dispatcher with routing and batch processing for VEX corpus."""
     2→
     3→import asyncio
     4→from collections import Counter
     5→from pathlib import Path
     6→from typing import Any
     7→
     8→from .client import OllamaClient
     9→from .models import (
    10→    BatchResult,
    11→    TaskResult,
    12→    TaskStatus,
    13→    TaskType,
    14→    TIER1_TASKS,
    15→    TIER2_TASKS,
    16→)
    17→
    18→
    19→class TaskDispatcher:
    20→    """Routes and dispatches VEX processing tasks to appropriate models."""
    21→
    22→    def __init__(
    23→        self,
    24→        client: OllamaClient | None = None,
    25→        config_path: Path | None = None,
    26→    ):
    27→        self.client = client or OllamaClient(config_path=config_path)
    28→        self._config = self.client.config
    29→
    30→    def get_tier(self, task_type: str | TaskType) -> int:

    32→        if isinstance(task_type, str):
    33→            try:
    34→                task_type = TaskType(task_type)
    35→            except ValueError:
    36→                return 1
    37→
    38→        if task_type in TIER1_TASKS:
    39→            return 1
    40→        elif task_type in TIER2_TASKS:
    41→            return 2
    42→        return 1
    43→
    44→    def get_model(self, task_type: str | TaskType) -> str:
    45→        """Get the primary model for a task type."""
    46→        tier = self.get_tier(task_type)
    47→        return self.client.get_model_for_tier(tier).primary
    48→
    49→    def should_use_consensus(self, task_type: str) -> bool:

    51→        task_config = self._config.get("tasks", {}).get(task_type, {})
    52→        return task_config.get("consensus", False)
    53→
    54→    async def dispatch(
    55→        self,
    56→        task_type: str,
    57→        input_data: dict[str, Any],
    58→        task_id: str = "",
    59→    ) -> TaskResult:
    60→        """Dispatch a single task to the appropriate model."""
    61→        if self.should_use_consensus(task_type):
    62→            return await self.dispatch_with_consensus(task_type, input_data, task_id)
    63→        return await self.client.process_task(task_type, input_data, task_id)
    64→
    65→    async def dispatch_with_consensus(
    66→        self,
    67→        task_type: str,
    68→        input_data: dict[str, Any],
    69→        task_id: str = "",
    70→    ) -> TaskResult:
    71→        """Dispatch task to multiple models and use consensus voting."""
    72→        tier = self.get_tier(task_type)
    73→        model_config = self.client.get_model_for_tier(tier)
    74→
    75→        # Get models to use for consensus
    76→        models = [model_config.primary] + model_config.fallbacks[:2]
    77→
    78→        # Run all models in parallel
    79→        tasks = [
    80→            self.client.process_task(task_type, input_data, task_id, model=m)
    81→            for m in models
    82→        ]
    83→        results = await asyncio.gather(*tasks, return_exceptions=True)
    84→
    85→        # Filter successful results
    86→        valid_results: list[TaskResult] = []
    87→        for r in results:
    88→            if isinstance(r, TaskResult) and r.status == TaskStatus.SUCCESS:
    89→                valid_results.append(r)
    90→
    91→        if not valid_results:
    92→            return TaskResult(
    93→                task_id=task_id,
    94→                status=TaskStatus.ERROR,
    95→                result={"error_type": "consensus_failed", "error_message": "No valid results"},
    96→            )
    97→
    98→        # Extract vote key based on task type
    99→        votes = []
   100→        for r in valid_results:
   101→            vote = self._extract_vote_key(task_type, r)
   102→            if vote is not None:
   103→                votes.append((vote, r))
   104→
   105→        if not votes:
   106→            return valid_results[0]
   107→
   108→        # Count votes
   109→        vote_counts = Counter(v[0] for v in votes)
   110→        winner, count = vote_counts.most_common(1)[0]
   111→        consensus_score = count / len(models)
   112→
   113→        # Find best matching result
   114→        for vote, result in votes:
   115→            if vote == winner:
   116→                result.result["consensus_score"] = consensus_score
   117→                result.processing_notes = (
   118→                    f"Consensus: {count}/{len(models)} models agreed"
   119→                )
   120→                return result
   121→
   122→        return valid_results[0]
   123→
   124→    def _extract_vote_key(self, task_type: str, result: TaskResult) -> Any:
   125→        """Extract the key field to vote on based on task type."""
   126→        r = result.result
   127→
   128→        if task_type == "classify_wrangle":
   129→            return r.get("context")
   130→        elif task_type == "classify_topic":
   131→            return r.get("primary_topic")
   132→        elif task_type == "rate_difficulty":
   133→            # Round to nearest 2 for fuzzy matching
   134→            diff = r.get("difficulty")
   135→            if diff is not None:
   136→                return round(diff / 2) * 2
   137→        elif task_type == "estimate_complexity":
   138→            return r.get("complexity")
   139→        elif task_type == "detect_bugs":
   140→            bugs = r.get("bugs", [])
   141→            return tuple(sorted(b.get("type", "") for b in bugs))
   142→
   143→        return None
   144→
   145→    async def dispatch_batch(
   146→        self,
   147→        task_type: str,
   148→        items: list[dict[str, Any]],
   149→        concurrency: int = 5,
   150→    ) -> BatchResult:
   151→        """Process a batch of items with concurrency control."""
   152→        semaphore = asyncio.Semaphore(concurrency)
   153→
   154→        async def process_item(item: dict[str, Any]) -> TaskResult:
   155→            async with semaphore:
   156→                item_id = item.get("id", "")
   157→                code = item.get("code", "")
   158→                return await self.dispatch(
   159→                    task_type,
   160→                    {"code": code, **{k: v for k, v in item.items() if k not in ("id", "code")}},
   161→                    task_id=item_id,
   162→                )
   163→
   164→        results = await asyncio.gather(*[process_item(item) for item in items])
   165→
   166→        # Compute stats
   167→        success_count = sum(1 for r in results if r.status == TaskStatus.SUCCESS)
   168→        error_count = sum(1 for r in results if r.status == TaskStatus.ERROR)
   169→        confidences = [r.confidence for r in results if r.status == TaskStatus.SUCCESS]
   170→        avg_confidence = sum(confidences) / len(confidences) if confidences else 0.0
   171→
   172→        return BatchResult(
   173→            results=list(results),
   174→            batch_stats={
   175→                "total": len(results),
   176→                "success": success_count,
   177→                "error": error_count,
   178→                "avg_confidence": round(avg_confidence, 3),
   179→            },
   180→        )
   181→
   182→    def should_flag_for_review(self, result: TaskResult) -> bool:
   183→        """Check if a result should be flagged for human review."""
   184→        quality_config = self._config.get("quality", {})
   185→        confidence_threshold = quality_config.get("flag_confidence_below", 0.6)
   186→        consensus_threshold = quality_config.get("flag_consensus_below", 0.66)
   187→
   188→        # Low confidence
   189→        if result.confidence < confidence_threshold:
   190→            return True
   191→
   192→        # Consensus failure
   193→        consensus_score = result.result.get("consensus_score", 1.0)
   194→        if consensus_score < consensus_threshold:
   195→            return True
   196→
   197→        # Error or uncertain status
   198→        if result.status in (TaskStatus.ERROR, TaskStatus.UNCERTAIN):
   199→            return True
   200→
   201→        return False
   202→
   203→    async def process_with_review(
   204→        self,
   205→        task_type: str,
   206→        items: list[dict[str, Any]],
   207→        concurrency: int = 5,
   208→    ) -> tuple[list[TaskResult], list[TaskResult]]:
   209→        """Process batch and separate results into passed and flagged."""
   210→        batch_result = await self.dispatch_batch(task_type, items, concurrency)
   211→
   212→        passed = []
   213→        flagged = []
   214→
   215→        for result in batch_result.results:
   216→            if self.should_flag_for_review(result):
   217→                flagged.append(result)
   218→            else:
   219→                passed.append(result)
   220→
   221→        return passed, flagged
   222→

1→#!/usr/bin/env python3
     2→"""
     3→Houdini Bridge - VEX Corpus Integration
     4→
     5→Connects to Houdini via hrpyc (Houdini Remote Python Connection) for
     6→bidirectional VEX code exchange.
     7→
     8→Houdini 21 uses hrpyc instead of the old command port:
     9→    - Default port: 18811
    10→    - Alternative: 9008 (if configured)
    11→
    12→Usage:
    13→    # In Houdini Python Shell, start the RPC server:
    14→    import hrpyc
    15→    hrpyc.start_server()  # Default port 18811
    16→    # Or: hrpyc.start_server(port=9008)
    17→
    18→    # Then from VEX Corpus:
    19→    python -m houdini.bridge --pull-all
    20→    python -m houdini.bridge --watch
    21→"""
    22→
    23→import asyncio
    24→import json
    25→import sys
    26→import time
    27→from pathlib import Path
    28→from typing import Optional, Callable, Any
    29→from dataclasses import dataclass, field
    30→from datetime import datetime
    31→from enum import Enum
    32→
    33→# Add parent to path for imports
    34→sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).parent.parent))
    35→
    36→
    37→# ============================================================================
    38→# Houdini Connection via hrpyc
    39→# ============================================================================
    40→
    41→class HoudiniConnectionError(Exception):
    42→    """Failed to connect to Houdini."""
    43→    pass
    44→
    45→
    46→class HoudiniConnection:
    47→    """
    48→    Connection to Houdini via hrpyc (Remote Python).
    49→
    50→    Houdini 21+ uses hrpyc instead of the old commandport.
    51→    The hrpyc module wraps the rpyc library for remote procedure calls.
    52→    """
    53→
    54→    def __init__(self, host: str = "127.0.0.1", port: int = 18811):
    55→        self.host = host
    56→        self.port = port
    57→        self._connection = None
    58→        self._hou = None  # Remote hou module
    59→        self._connected = False
    60→
    61→    def connect(self) -> bool:
    62→        """Establish connection to Houdini via hrpyc."""
    63→        try:
    64→            import rpyc
    65→        except ImportError:
    66→            raise HoudiniConnectionError(
    67→                "rpyc module not installed. Install with: pip install rpyc"
    68→            )
    69→
    70→        try:
    71→            # Connect to Houdini's hrpyc server
    72→            self._connection = rpyc.classic.connect(self.host, self.port)
    73→
    74→            # Import remote hou module
    75→            self._hou = self._connection.modules.hou
    76→
    77→            # Test the connection
    78→            _ = self._hou.applicationVersion()
    79→
    80→            self._connected = True
    81→            print(f"[HOUDINI] Connected via hrpyc at {self.host}:{self.port}")
    82→            return True
    83→
    84→        except ConnectionRefusedError:
    85→            raise HoudiniConnectionError(
    86→                f"Cannot connect to Houdini at {self.host}:{self.port}.\n"
    87→                f"Make sure Houdini is running with hrpyc server enabled:\n"
    88→                f"  In Houdini Python Shell:\n"
    89→                f"    import hrpyc\n"
    90→                f"    hrpyc.start_server(port={self.port})"
    91→            )
    92→        except Exception as e:
    93→            raise HoudiniConnectionError(f"Connection failed: {e}")
    94→
    95→    def disconnect(self):
    96→        """Close the connection."""
    97→        if self._connection:
    98→            try:
    99→                self._connection.close()
   100→            except:
   101→                pass
   102→        self._connection = None
   103→        self._hou = None
   104→        self._connected = False
   105→
   106→    @property
   107→    def hou(self):
   108→        """Get the remote hou module."""
   109→        if not self._connected:
   110→            raise HoudiniConnectionError("Not connected to Houdini")
   111→        return self._hou
   112→
   113→    def execute(self, code: str) -> Any:
   114→        """Execute Python code in Houdini and return result."""
   115→        if not self._connected:
   116→            raise HoudiniConnectionError("Not connected to Houdini")
   117→
   118→        # Execute in Houdini's namespace
   119→        return self._connection.execute(code)
   120→
   121→
   122→# ============================================================================
   123→# VEX Extraction
   124→# ============================================================================
   125→
   126→@dataclass
   127→class HoudiniVEXNode:
   128→    """Represents a VEX-containing node in Houdini."""
   129→    path: str                    # Full node path, e.g., /obj/geo1/attribwrangle1
   130→    name: str                    # Node name
   131→    node_type: str               # e.g., "attribwrangle", "volumewrangle"
   132→    context: str                 # "points", "prims", "vertices", "detail"
   133→    vex_code: str                # The actual VEX code
   134→    parameters: dict = field(default_factory=dict)
   135→
   136→
   137→class HoudiniVEXExtractor:
   138→    """
   139→    Extracts VEX code from nodes in a Houdini scene.
   140→
   141→    Supported node types:
   142→    - attribwrangle (Point/Prim/Vertex/Detail Wrangle)
   143→    - volumewrangle
   144→    - popwrangle
   145→    - geometryvop (inline VEX)
   146→    """
   147→
   148→    WRANGLE_TYPES = ["attribwrangle", "volumewrangle", "popwrangle", "gaswrangle"]
   149→
   150→    def __init__(self, connection: HoudiniConnection):
   151→        self.conn = connection
   152→
   153→    def _get_context(self, node) -> str:
   154→        """Determine wrangle context from class parameter."""
   155→        try:
   156→            cls_parm = node.parm("class")
   157→            if cls_parm:
   158→                val = cls_parm.evalAsInt()
   159→                return {0: "detail", 1: "points", 2: "prims", 3: "vertices"}.get(val, "points")
   160→        except:
   161→            pass
   162→        return "points"
   163→
   164→    def find_all_wrangles(self) -> list[HoudiniVEXNode]:
   165→        """Find all wrangle nodes in the current scene."""
   166→        hou = self.conn.hou
   167→        results = []
   168→
   169→        try:
   170→            root = hou.node("/")
   171→            for node in root.allSubChildren():
   172→                try:
   173→                    type_name = node.type().name()
   174→
   175→                    if any(wt in type_name for wt in self.WRANGLE_TYPES):
   176→                        snippet_parm = node.parm("snippet")
   177→                        if snippet_parm:
   178→                            code = snippet_parm.evalAsString()
   179→                            if code and code.strip():
   180→                                results.append(HoudiniVEXNode(
   181→                                    path=node.path(),
   182→                                    name=node.name(),
   183→                                    node_type=type_name,
   184→                                    context=self._get_context(node),
   185→                                    vex_code=code
   186→                                ))
   187→                except Exception:
   188→                    continue
   189→
   190→        except Exception as e:
   191→            print(f"[HOUDINI] Error finding wrangles: {e}")
   192→
   193→        return results
   194→
   195→    def get_node_vex(self, node_path: str) -> Optional[HoudiniVEXNode]:
   196→        """Get VEX code from a specific node."""
   197→        hou = self.conn.hou
   198→
   199→        try:
   200→            node = hou.node(node_path)
   201→            if node:
   202→                snippet = node.parm("snippet")
   203→                if snippet:
   204→                    return HoudiniVEXNode(
   205→                        path=node.path(),
   206→                        name=node.name(),
   207→                        node_type=node.type().name(),
   208→                        context=self._get_context(node),
   209→                        vex_code=snippet.evalAsString()
   210→                    )
   211→        except Exception as e:
   212→            print(f"[HOUDINI] Error getting node VEX: {e}")
   213→
   214→        return None
   215→
   216→    def set_node_vex(self, node_path: str, vex_code: str) -> bool:
   217→        """Set VEX code on a specific node."""
   218→        hou = self.conn.hou
   219→
   220→        try:
   221→            node = hou.node(node_path)
   222→            if node:
   223→                snippet = node.parm("snippet")
   224→                if snippet:
   225→                    snippet.set(vex_code)
   226→                    return True
   227→        except Exception as e:
   228→            print(f"[HOUDINI] Error setting node VEX: {e}")
   229→
   230→        return False
   231→
   232→
   233→# ============================================================================
   234→# Houdini Bridge (High-Level Interface)
   235→# ============================================================================
   236→
   237→class HoudiniBridge:
   238→    """
   239→    High-level interface between VEX Corpus and Houdini.
   240→
   241→    Provides:
   242→    - Pull VEX from all wrangles in scene
   243→    - Push VEX to specific nodes
   244→    - Watch for changes (polling)
   245→    - Queue samples directly to the corpus pipeline
   246→    """
   247→
   248→    def __init__(self,
   249→                 host: str = "127.0.0.1",
   250→                 port: int = 18811,
   251→                 corpus_callback: Optional[Callable] = None):
   252→        """
   253→        Initialize bridge.
   254→
   255→        Args:
   256→            host: Houdini host (usually localhost)
   257→            port: hrpyc port (default 18811)
   258→            corpus_callback: Called with VEXSample when new code is found
   259→        """
   260→        self.host = host
   261→        self.port = port
   262→        self.corpus_callback = corpus_callback
   263→
   264→        self._conn: Optional[HoudiniConnection] = None
   265→        self._extractor: Optional[HoudiniVEXExtractor] = None
   266→        self._connected = False
   267→        self._watching = False
   268→
   269→        # Track seen code to avoid duplicates
   270→        self._seen_hashes: set[str] = set()
   271→        self._node_versions: dict[str, str] = {}  # path -> hash of code
   272→
   273→    def connect(self) -> bool:
   274→        """Connect to Houdini."""
   275→        try:
   276→            self._conn = HoudiniConnection(self.host, self.port)
   277→            self._conn.connect()
   278→            self._extractor = HoudiniVEXExtractor(self._conn)
   279→            self._connected = True
   280→            return True
   281→        except HoudiniConnectionError as e:
   282→            print(f"[HOUDINI] {e}")
   283→            self._connected = False
   284→            return False
   285→
   286→    def disconnect(self):
   287→        """Disconnect from Houdini."""
   288→        if self._conn:
   289→            self._conn.disconnect()
   290→        self._connected = False
   291→        self._watching = False
   292→        print("[HOUDINI] Disconnected")
   293→
   294→    def is_connected(self) -> bool:
   295→        """Check if connected to Houdini."""
   296→        return self._connected
   297→
   298→    def pull_all_vex(self) -> list[HoudiniVEXNode]:
   299→        """Pull all VEX code from the current Houdini scene."""
   300→        if not self._connected:
   301→            print("[HOUDINI] Not connected")
   302→            return []
   303→
   304→        nodes = self._extractor.find_all_wrangles()
   305→        print(f"[HOUDINI] Found {len(nodes)} wrangle nodes")
   306→        return nodes
   307→
   308→    def pull_node(self, node_path: str) -> Optional[HoudiniVEXNode]:
   309→        """Pull VEX from a specific node."""
   310→        if not self._connected:
   311→            return None
   312→        return self._extractor.get_node_vex(node_path)
   313→
   314→    def push_vex(self, node_path: str, vex_code: str) -> bool:
   315→        """Push VEX code to a specific node."""
   316→        if not self._connected:
   317→            return False
   318→        return self._extractor.set_node_vex(node_path, vex_code)
   319→
   320→    def _hash_code(self, code: str) -> str:
   321→        """Generate hash for deduplication."""
   322→        import hashlib
   323→        return hashlib.sha256(code.encode()).hexdigest()[:16]
   324→
   325→    def ingest_to_corpus(self, nodes: list[HoudiniVEXNode] = None):
   326→        """
   327→        Send VEX nodes to the corpus for processing.
   328→
   329→        If no nodes provided, pulls all from Houdini.
   330→        """

   338→        # Import here to avoid circular dependency
   339→        from pipeline.intake import VEXSample, ProcessingStage
   340→
   341→        new_samples = []
   342→        for node in nodes:
   343→            code_hash = self._hash_code(node.vex_code)
   344→
   345→            if code_hash in self._seen_hashes:
   346→                continue
   347→
   348→            self._seen_hashes.add(code_hash)
   349→
   350→            sample = VEXSample(
   351→                id=f"houdini_{code_hash}",
   352→                code=node.vex_code,
   353→                source_file=f"houdini://{node.path}",
   354→                source_line=0,
   355→                hash=code_hash,
   356→                context=node.context,
   357→                stage=ProcessingStage.PENDING

   360→            new_samples.append(sample)
   361→
   362→            if self.corpus_callback:

   365→        print(f"[HOUDINI] Ingested {len(new_samples)} new samples to corpus")
   366→        return new_samples

   368→    async def watch(self, interval: float = 2.0):
   369→        """
   370→        Watch Houdini for VEX changes and auto-ingest.
   371→
   372→        Polls every `interval` seconds for new/modified wrangles.
   373→        """
   374→        if not self._connected:
   375→            print("[HOUDINI] Not connected - cannot watch")
   376→            return
   377→
   378→        self._watching = True
   379→        print(f"[HOUDINI] Watching for changes (every {interval}s)...")
   380→
   381→        while self._watching:
   382→            try:
   383→                nodes = self.pull_all_vex()
   384→
   385→                for node in nodes:
   386→                    code_hash = self._hash_code(node.vex_code)
   387→
   388→                    # Check if this node's code changed
   389→                    if self._node_versions.get(node.path) != code_hash:
   390→                        self._node_versions[node.path] = code_hash
   391→

   393→                            self._seen_hashes.add(code_hash)
   394→
   395→                            print(f"[HOUDINI] New/modified: {node.path}")
   396→
   397→                            # Ingest single node
   398→                            self.ingest_to_corpus([node])
   399→
   400→            except Exception as e:
   401→                print(f"[HOUDINI] Watch error: {e}")

   403→            await asyncio.sleep(interval)

   414→class HoudiniSubagent:
   415→    """
   416→    Async subagent that integrates with the VEX Corpus orchestrator.
   417→
   418→    Runs alongside other subagents, feeding samples from Houdini
   419→    directly into the processing pipeline.
   420→    """
   421→
   422→    def __init__(self, orchestrator, host: str = "127.0.0.1", port: int = 18811):
   423→        self.orchestrator = orchestrator
   424→        self.host = host
   425→        self.port = port
   426→        self.bridge: Optional[HoudiniBridge] = None
   427→        self._running = False
   428→        self._task: Optional[asyncio.Task] = None
   429→
   430→        # Metrics
   431→        self.samples_pulled = 0
   432→        self.last_pull = None
   433→
   434→    async def start(self):
   435→        """Start the Houdini subagent."""
   436→        self._running = True
   437→
   438→        # Create bridge with callback to orchestrator
   439→        self.bridge = HoudiniBridge(
   440→            host=self.host,
   441→            port=self.port,
   442→            corpus_callback=self._on_sample
   443→        )
   444→
   445→        if not self.bridge.connect():
   446→            print("[HOUDINI-AGENT] Could not connect - will retry periodically")
   447→
   448→        self._task = asyncio.create_task(self._run())
   449→
   450→    async def stop(self):
   451→        """Stop the subagent."""
   452→        self._running = False
   453→
   454→        if self.bridge:
   455→            self.bridge.stop_watching()
   456→            self.bridge.disconnect()
   457→
   458→        if self._task:
   459→            self._task.cancel()
   460→            try:
   461→                await self._task
   462→            except asyncio.CancelledError:
   463→                pass
   464→
   465→    async def _run(self):
   466→        """Main run loop - watch for Houdini changes."""
   467→        reconnect_interval = 10.0
   468→        watch_interval = 2.0
   469→
   470→        while self._running:
   471→            try:
   472→                if not self.bridge.is_connected():
   473→                    # Try to connect
   474→                    if self.bridge.connect():
   475→                        print("[HOUDINI-AGENT] Connected!")
   476→                    else:
   477→                        await asyncio.sleep(reconnect_interval)
   478→                        continue
   479→
   480→                # Poll for changes
   481→                nodes = self.bridge.pull_all_vex()
   482→
   483→                for node in nodes:
   484→                    code_hash = self.bridge._hash_code(node.vex_code)
   485→
   486→                    if code_hash not in self.bridge._seen_hashes:
   487→                        self.bridge._seen_hashes.add(code_hash)
   488→                        self._queue_sample(node, code_hash)
   489→                        self.samples_pulled += 1
   490→                        self.last_pull = datetime.now()
   491→
   492→                await asyncio.sleep(watch_interval)
   493→
   494→            except Exception as e:
   495→                print(f"[HOUDINI-AGENT] Error: {e}")
   496→                # Mark as disconnected on error
   497→                if self.bridge:
   498→                    self.bridge._connected = False
   499→                await asyncio.sleep(reconnect_interval)
   500→
   501→    def _on_sample(self, sample):
   502→        """Callback when bridge finds a sample."""
   503→        # Queue to orchestrator
   504→        if hasattr(self.orchestrator, 'tier1_queue'):
   505→            asyncio.create_task(self.orchestrator.tier1_queue.put(sample))
   506→            self.orchestrator.metrics.total_ingested += 1
   507→
   508→    def _queue_sample(self, node: HoudiniVEXNode, code_hash: str):
   509→        """Queue a sample to the orchestrator."""
   510→        from pipeline.intake import VEXSample, ProcessingStage
   511→
   512→        sample = VEXSample(
   513→            id=f"houdini_{code_hash}",
   514→            code=node.vex_code,
   515→            source_file=f"houdini://{node.path}",
   516→            source_line=0,
   517→            hash=code_hash,
   518→            context=node.context,
   519→            stage=ProcessingStage.PENDING
   520→        )
   521→
   522→        # Add to orchestrator tracking
   523→        if hasattr(self.orchestrator, 'samples'):
   524→            self.orchestrator.samples[sample.id] = sample
   525→            self.orchestrator.seen_hashes.add(code_hash)
   526→
   527→        # Queue for processing
   528→        asyncio.create_task(self.orchestrator.tier1_queue.put(sample))
   529→
   530→        if hasattr(self.orchestrator, 'metrics'):
   531→            self.orchestrator.metrics.total_ingested += 1
   532→
   533→        print(f"[HOUDINI-AGENT] Queued: {node.path} ({node.context})")
   534→

    29→class ProcessingWorker(QThread):
    30→    """Background worker for async pipeline processing."""

    32→    progress = pyqtSignal(str, int, int)  # stage, current, total
    33→    sample_complete = pyqtSignal(object)  # VEXSample
    34→    error = pyqtSignal(str, str)  # source, message

    38→    def __init__(self, pipeline: IntakePipeline, sources: list):

    41→        self.sources = sources  # List of (type, path) tuples
    42→        self._cancelled = False

    44→    def cancel(self):

    47→    def run(self):
    48→        loop = asyncio.new_event_loop()
    49→        asyncio.set_event_loop(loop)
    50→
    51→        try:
    52→            # Connect callbacks
    53→            self.pipeline.on_progress(
    54→                lambda stage, cur, tot: self.progress.emit(stage, cur, tot)
    55→            )
    56→            self.pipeline.on_sample_complete(
    57→                lambda s: self.sample_complete.emit(s)
    58→            )
    59→            self.pipeline.on_error(
    60→                lambda src, e: self.error.emit(src, str(e))
    61→            )
    62→
    63→            all_samples = []
    64→
    65→            # Ingest from all sources
    66→            for source_type, source_path in self.sources:
    67→                if self._cancelled:
    68→                    break
    69→
    70→                self.log.emit(f"Ingesting from {source_path}...")
    71→
    72→                if source_type == "file":
    73→                    samples = loop.run_until_complete(
    74→                        self.pipeline.ingest_file(Path(source_path))
    75→                    )
    76→                elif source_type == "directory":
    77→                    samples = loop.run_until_complete(
    78→                        self.pipeline.ingest_directory(Path(source_path))
    79→                    )
    80→                elif source_type == "code":
    81→                    sample = loop.run_until_complete(
    82→                        self.pipeline.ingest_code(source_path)
    83→                    )
    84→                    samples = [sample]
    85→                else:
    86→                    continue
    87→
    88→                all_samples.extend(samples)
    89→                self.log.emit(f"  Found {len(samples)} samples")
    90→
    91→            if self._cancelled:
    92→                self.log.emit("Processing cancelled.")
    93→                self.finished.emit([])
    94→                return
    95→
    96→            self.log.emit(f"\nTotal samples to process: {len(all_samples)}")
    97→
    98→            # Process through pipeline

   105→                self.finished.emit(processed)
